title: Sex After Birth: When and How to Resume Intimacy Postpartum

description: When to resume sex after birth is the most common question. Read this blog to get an idea of when to start and have a healthy sexual life.

html:
Having sex after birth is not the same as before having a baby. Pregnancy and having a baby can change a lot in your body, including your sex life. Once you have a newborn, you might need to settle into a new routine, and among those complications, the last one that comes to your mind may be sex. 

To maintain a healthier and safer sexual life after birth, you first need to give your body some time off after delivery, and there is no actual timeline to definitively say how long you should wait to have sex after birth because the waiting time depends on the type of delivery and other factors. All those factors and how to resume intimacy after birth are explained in this blog post.

How Type of Delivery Impacts Sex After Birth

Sex after birth needs recovery and healing for the body. So, how soon you can resume sexual intimacy after birth varies from person to person based on the type of delivery, like vaginal or cesarean.

1. Sex After a Vaginal Birth

Vaginal delivery causes stretching and, in very rare cases, possible tearing of the perineal area. So, it requires stitches and time to heal. Also, there are other common postpartum issues, such as vaginal dryness, perineal pain, and lochia (post-birth vaginal bleeding), that can make resuming sex uncomfortable or even painful.

How long should you wait?

  • Most healthcare providers recommend 4 to 6 weeks of waiting time before resuming sex after a vaginal birth. This time allows vaginal tissues to heal and stops bleeding. 
  • If you had a perineal tear or episiotomy, then additional healing time might be needed.

Factors to consider

Even after the recommended period by your healthcare provider, you must consider some factors before having sex. If you are having any, never start having intimacy without consulting a healthcare provider. They are,

  • The severity of perineal tearing
  • The presence of pain or discomfort
  • Vaginal dryness due to hormonal changes
  • Emotional readiness and fatigue from caring for a newborn

2. Sex After a Cesarean (C-Section)

In comparison with vaginal delivery C-section is a major abdominal surgery which requires more time to heal. C-section causes incision pain, limited mobility, and postpartum fatigue that impacts sexual desire and comfort.

How long should you wait?

  • Doctors typically recommend waiting 6 to 8 weeks before engaging in sexual activity to allow the incision site to heal properly and reduce the risk of infection.
  • Hormonal shifts after birth might cause vaginal dryness and low libido due to hormonal shifts.

Factors to consider

Before having sex after birth through C-section, you might consider some factors. They are,

  • Pain at the incision site
  • Core muscle weakness and limited movement
  • Possible scar tenderness
  • The emotional impact of the birth experience

Factors That Influence When to Resume Sex After Birth

Your doctors might recommend some days to wait before having sex. Even after that, there are several factors to consider before resuming intimacy. Giving importance to emotional and psychological readiness is equally important to physical recovery.

1. Physical Recovery

Your physicality before birth and after birth are entirely very different as the body undergoes immense changes during pregnancy and childbirth. Healing time varies depending on the below factors,

  • The extent of vaginal tearing or C-section incision healing
  • The presence of postpartum bleeding (lochia)
  • Pelvic floor strength and vaginal elasticity

2. Hormonal Changes

After giving birth to a newborn, estrogen levels drop and it leads to vaginal dryness, which makes sex uncomfortable or painful. Breastfeeding can further reduce estrogen levels and delay natural lubrication.

3. Emotional Readiness and Mental Health

Many new mothers experience postpartum blues or depression, which can affect sexual desire. Feelings of exhaustion, anxiety, or stress can also reduce interest in intimacy.

4. Sleep Deprivation and Fatigue

Caring for a newborn is physically and emotionally demanding. The first few months after having a baby are really tough as your routine changes to changing diapers, sleepless nights, feeding and taking care of the baby. Lack of sleep and energy can make sex feel like an added chore rather than an enjoyable activity.

5.Relationship Dynamics

Adjusting to parenthood can put a strain on relationships. Open communication between partners is crucial in understanding each other’s emotional and physical needs.

When to See a Doctor

If you are having any of the following issues, consult your healthcare provider before resuming sexual activity. 

  • Severe pain during sex
  • Persistent vaginal bleeding or unusual discharge
  • Signs of infection (fever, foul-smelling discharge, or swelling)
  • Incontinence or pelvic floor weakness affecting sexual function

Takeaway

Resuming sex after birth cannot be done immediately as the body changes after giving birth, and it requires healing time based on the type of delivery. Also, emotional and psychological recovery, along with physical recovery, should be considered. Open communication, patience and self-care are the keys to restoring intimacy postpartum. title: Why Do Guys Feel Bad After Ejaculating?

description: Most men feel guilty or messy after ejaculation due to certain causes. Those causes and how to overcome those causes are explained in this post.

html:
There is a common issue that most men report as they are having a bad feeling after an ejaculation, either alone or with their sexual partner. This issue needs to be reported if you are having it consistently because the bad feeling can make ejaculation an avoidable activity. Finding out the reason that makes you feel bad after ejaculation and getting rid of them is necessary. No worries, as this blog post explains the most commonly reported reasons that make a man feel bad after ejaculation, how to overcome the bad feelings, and when to seek professionals.

Causes of feeling bad after ejaculation

The causes that make a man feel bad after ejaculation can be divided into two different categories. They are,

  1. Psychological Causes of Feeling Bad After Ejaculation
  2. Physical Causes of Post-Ejaculation Discomfort

Psychological Causes of Feeling Bad After Ejaculation

  • Post-Coital Dysphoria (PCD)
  • Guilt and Shame
  • Relationship Concerns
  • Depression and Anxiety

Post-Coital Dysphoria (PCD)

Post-coital dysphoria (PCD) is a condition also called post-sex blues, where a man experiences sadness, anxiety, irritability, or depression after ejaculation. This emotional response can last anywhere from a few minutes to several hours. There is no proper, fully done research on PCD. However, some research available on the web says that hormonal changes, neurotransmitter fluctuations, and psychological factors contribute to this condition.

Guilt and Shame

Many men are brought up with the teachings that say never ejaculate until marriage; likewise, there are some cultural beliefs, personal morality, and cultural influences. They are,

  • Religious Beliefs: Some religions teach that masturbation or sex outside of marriage is sinful. This leads to a guilty feeling after ejaculation.
  • Personal Morality: Men feel bad after having a relationship with a woman who they never wanted. Most men like having orgasms with the partner they are in a long-term relationship with.
  • Cultural Influences: Societal pressures around masculinity, purity, or self-control may cause men to feel regret after sexual release.

Relationship Concerns

Men in relationships may experience negative feelings after ejaculation due to emotional or psychological reasons such as:

  • Guilt over infidelity (physical or emotional)
  • Not having a good emotional connection with a partner.
  • Conflict in a Relationship or an unsatisfied relationship 
  • Feeling like being used or using someone else.

Depression and Anxiety

Suppose a man has mental health conditions like depression and anxiety. In that case, it may contribute to negative thought patterns, self-criticism, or general feelings of sadness after having an orgasm. 

Physical Causes of Post-Ejaculation Discomfort

  • Hormonal Changes
  • Post-Orgasmic Illness Syndrome (POIS)
  • Dehydration and Nutrient Loss

Hormonal Changes

After ejaculation, the body releases various hormones, including dopamine, oxytocin, and prolactin. If there is a sudden drop in dopamine and oxytocin after orgasm, then it can lead to feelings of sadness or emptiness. 

Also, research suggests that after an orgasm, some men experience a drop in Serotonin. It is a neurotransmitter in the brain that helps in maintaining happiness. Also, a drop in Prolactin contributes to temporary emotional distress as it is responsible for post-orgasmic relaxation.

Post-Orgasmic Illness Syndrome (POIS)

POIS is a rare condition and also not reported by many men, where a man experiences flu-like symptoms after ejaculation, but there might not be any flu on him. It includes, 

  • Fatigue
  • Muscle aches
  • Brain fog
  • Irritability or mood swings

The exact cause of POIS is unclear, but it is believed to be an autoimmune or allergic response to one’s semen.

Dehydration and Nutrient Loss

After ejaculation, there will be a loss of fluids and nutrients like magnesium and zinc from the man’s body. So, if he is not sufficiently hydrated and has these nutrients, he may feel bad after ejaculation because he will become weak, tired, or mentally foggy.

How to Overcome Negative Feelings After Ejaculation

Overcoming negative feelings after ejaculation for a male is complicated as you need to find the root cause of these feelings and improve yourself by making your self-image stronger is the most important. So, consider asking yourself to overcome the guilt, shame, or anxiety that is contributing to your post-ejaculatory distress. If you are unable to find them, then consulting with a therapist or counselor can be very helpful in finding and solving the issue.

To make yourself mentally stronger. Follow self-compassion and understand that sexual activities are natural and that experiencing them is not shameful. To be physically fit, you need to have a well-hydrated body and a balanced diet.

If you are well and your relationship with your partner is not well-strengthened, it might cause bad feelings. So, take steps like discussing feelings, expectations, and emotional needs to build a stronger connection.

Other ways are to be physically fit, exercise regularly, consider taking supplements if you lack nutrients, and get sufficient sleep.

When to Seek Professional Help

Suppose feelings of sadness, guilt, or discomfort after ejaculation are persistent and interfere with your daily life. Then, you must seek professional help. If you are confused about reaching the doctor, follow the details below. 

  • Sex Therapist: To address psychological and emotional concerns related to sex.
  • Psychologist or Psychiatrist: If anxiety, depression, or trauma plays a role.
  • Urologist: If there are physical symptoms like POIS or extreme fatigue after ejaculation.

Takeaway

Feeling bad after ejaculation is reported more widely by men than women. No worries; you need to ask yourself questions to find out the root cause of the bad feeling you are having and solve it by making yourself a strong individual against the feeling that makes you bad. Be physically and mentally fit to avoid bad feelings after orgasm. If you are having this bad feeling consistently for a longer period, consult with a sexual health doctor or psychologist to get a solution.

title: How To Improve Sex Time?: 9 Tips For Men

html:
The term stamina in the sexual health of a man stands for how many minutes you last in bed with your partner. So, if you stay in bed longer with your female partner, you have very good stamina. Having stamina can increase the sexual pleasure of you and your partner. Focusing on sexual performance can bring anxiety to almost every man. So, to avoid the opposing sides of sexual performance with your partner, following some lifestyle changes is enough. Read more to know the tips to improve sexual stamina and sex time.

This post explains the nine practical tips that can help you find answers to questions like “how to have sex for a long time” and “how to increase sex stamina.” 

  1. Prioritize Physical Fitness
  2. Maintain a Balanced Diet
  3. Manage Stress and Anxiety
  4. Practice Kegel Exercises
  5. Explore the Start-Stop Technique
  6. Consider the Squeeze Technique
  7. Limit Alcohol and Avoid Smoking
  8. Get Adequate Sleep
  9. Consult a Healthcare Professional

1. Prioritize Physical Fitness

Physical fitness is essential in improving a man’s sexual stamina. Cardiovascular workouts, strength training, and flexibility exercises can enhance endurance, circulation, and overall energy levels.

  • Cardio Workouts like running, cycling, and swimming boost heart health and ensure better blood flow for stronger and longer-lasting erections.
  • Strength Training, such as squats, deadlifts, and planks, is beneficial as it strengthens the core, lower body, and pelvic muscles, improving thrust control and stamina. However, to avoid injuries, strength training requires professional guidance. 
  • Flexibility Exercises such as yoga and stretching enhance mobility, reducing muscle tension and improving movement during intercourse.

Adding these three types of exercises to your regular exercise routine can build you the endurance needed for longer-lasting in bed. These exercises can also increase testosterone levels, which play a crucial role in libido and performance.

2. Maintain a Balanced Diet

It’s not a big surprise that nutrition plays a direct role in sexual health. A well-balanced diet provides essential nutrients that support stamina, energy, and overall performance. Here are some sex drive foods for males.

  • Intake of fruits and vegetables high in antioxidants improves blood circulation and reduces inflammation.
  • Lean Proteins such as chicken, fish, and legumes help build muscle strength and sustain energy levels.
  • Whole Grains provide long-lasting energy and maintain stable blood sugar levels, reducing fatigue.
  • Healthy fats from nuts, seeds, and fish promote heart health and improve circulation, ensuring better erectile function.

Not only consuming these foods but also avoiding foods like processed foods, excessive sugar, and unhealthy fat can prevent energy crashes and weight gain. If you are regularly consuming unhealthy foods, it may also lead to sexual dysfunction.

3. Manage Stress and Anxiety

If you are not lasting longer in bed, then it could cause performance anxiety. Having anxiety could not give you the performance you needed. Having stress triggers the release of cortisol, which can interfere with testosterone production and lead to premature ejaculation or erectile dysfunction.

  • Practicing meditation helps in calming the mind, reducing stress and anxiety before intimacy.
  • Deep Breathing Techniques promote relaxation and enhance focus, allowing better control over-arousal.
  • Open Communication with a partner can ease pressure and create a more relaxed and enjoyable experience.

Do hobbies that relieve you from stress and also follow other techniques so that you can have an improved and satisfied sexual performance.

4. Practice Kegel Exercises

Kegel exercise is recommended by almost every professional male sexologist to improve male performance in bed. Kegel exercises strengthen the pelvic floor muscles, which are key in controlling ejaculation and enhancing stamina. Having a strong pelvic floor allows men to delay climax and enjoy longer-lasting pleasure.

Regularly practicing Kegels can lead to improved control over ejaculation and stronger erections. Over time, this simple exercise can significantly enhance sexual endurance.

5. Start-Stop Technique

The start-stop method is an effective way to build better control over ejaculation. It involves stimulating the penis until nearing climax, then stopping and allowing arousal to decrease before resuming.

Practicing this technique regularly can train the body to delay orgasm, resulting in prolonged intercourse and increased pleasure for both partners. It is beneficial for men who experience premature ejaculation.

6. Squeeze Technique

Similar to the start-stop method, the squeeze technique involves gently pressing the base of the penis when ejaculation feels imminent. This momentarily reduces arousal and allows for better control over climax timing.

By incorporating this technique during intercourse or foreplay, men can train themselves to last longer and improve their sexual stamina over time.

7. Limit Alcohol and Avoid Smoking

Following unhealthy habits such as excessive alcohol consumption and Smoking can negatively affect sexual performance by impairing circulation and reducing testosterone levels.

  • Alcohol slows down the nervous system. which leads to decreased sensitivity and weaker erections.
  • Smoking restricts blood flow. Which makes it harder to achieve and maintain erections.

Reducing or eliminating these habits can lead to better sexual health, increased stamina, and improved overall well-being.

8. Get Adequate Sleep

Sleep plays a vital role in the body’s overall functioning, including sexual functions. Adequate sleep makes hormone regulations effective. Lack of sleep can lead to fatigue, stress, and decreased testosterone production, negatively impacting stamina.  

  • Aim for 7-9 hours of sleep daily to ensure optimal hormonal balance and energy levels.
  • Establishing a consistent sleep schedule and creating a relaxing bedtime routine can further enhance physical and sexual performance.

9. Consult a Healthcare Professional

Even though by following all the techniques, you are still lacking in stamina then, consulting a male sexologist can be better. Because they help you in identifying the presence of any sexual dysfunction conditions like low testosterone, erectile dysfunction, or anxiety disorders.

  • A male sexologist can recommend medical treatments, therapy, or supplements that may help improve endurance and overall sexual health.
  • Addressing concerns early can prevent long-term issues and enhance confidence in intimate relationships.

Takeaway

Improving sexual stamina is a gradual process that involves a combination of physical fitness, a balanced diet, stress management, and mindful sexual techniques. By following these simple lifestyle changes, men can naturally boost their endurance, enhance pleasure, and build confidence in bed with their partners. Also, when no techniques are working, consulting a male sexual doctor is needed. html:
Yes, drinking water benefits both men and women sexually. The role of water is vital in the performance of our overall health, and it also benefits us sexually by helping us avoid erectile dysfunction, as dehydration could lead to erectile dysfunction. You can prevent treatment to improve your sexual performance if you are keeping yourself hydrated. 

There are some important roles that water plays in sexual performance that are explained in this blog post, along with the answers to the question of whether we should drink water just before sex and the problems caused by dehydration to our sexual health.

How being hydrated improves sexual performance

Drinking water helps you to be hydrated, and being hydrated helps you to improve sexual performance. The benefits are, 

  1. Improves Blood circulation
  2. Prevents Erectile Dysfunction
  3. Boosts Libido and Stamina
  4. Enhances Natural Lubrication
  5. Flushes Out Toxins
  6. Reduces Stress and Anxiety
  7. Improves Sperm Quality and Fertility

1. Improves Blood Circulation

Good blood flow is essential for arousal and sexual performance. Water helps maintain proper circulation by ensuring that oxygen and nutrients reach all parts of the body, including our reproductive organs. For men, proper blood flow is necessary for achieving and maintaining an erection, while for women, it enhances sensitivity and lubrication.

2. Prevents Erectile Dysfunction

One of the lesser-known causes of erectile dysfunction (ED) is dehydration. The lack of water in the body makes the blood volume decrease, and it makes it difficult for the heart to pump sufficient blood to the penis. This can lead to weak or short-lived erections. By being hydrated, a man can reduce the risk of ED, and if you are already being affected by ED, then drinking sufficient water could reduce the effects of ED.

3. Boosts Libido and Stamina

Fatigue and low energy levels can negatively impact sexual desire and performance. Water helps regulate the proper functioning of metabolism and energy production. When you are hydrated, your body functions optimally, allowing you to maintain stamina and enjoy longer-lasting intimacy.

4. Enhances Natural Lubrication

For women, dehydration can cause vaginal dryness, leading to discomfort and pain during intercourse. Drinking enough water ensures natural lubrication, making intimate moments more enjoyable and reducing the need for artificial lubricants.

5. Flushes Out Toxins

Toxins in the body can lead to hormonal imbalances and reduced sexual desire. Drinking water helps flush out these toxins, ensuring that your reproductive system functions correctly and that your hormones remain balanced.

6. Reduces Stress and Anxiety

Stress and anxiety can be significant barriers to a satisfying sex life. Dehydration can increase cortisol (the stress hormone) levels, making you feel more anxious and less interested in sex. Staying hydrated keeps your body and mind calm, allowing for a more relaxed and pleasurable experience.

7. Improves Sperm Quality and Fertility

Hydration plays a vital role in sperm production and quality for men looking to conceive. Water is essential for semen production, and dehydration can lead to lower sperm count and motility. By drinking enough water, men can improve their fertility and reproductive health.

Should You Drink Water Before Sex?

Many people wonder whether drinking water just before sex is beneficial. The answer is yes but in moderation. 

The moderate answer is that drinking a small amount of water before intimacy can keep you hydrated, prevent dryness, and improve stamina. However, consuming too much water right before sex may cause bloating or discomfort. It is best to maintain consistent hydration throughout the day rather than relying on last-minute water intake.

Problems Caused by Dehydration in Sexual Health

1. Reduced Sexual Desire

Dehydration reduces the blood volume in the body, which causes fatigue, headaches, and low energy levels. These effects combine and have a negative effect on our libido. The body does not prioritize sexual desire when it lacks water; it only prioritizes essential functions.

2. Weaker Erections

Lack of blood volume due to dehydration causes the brain cells to lack in sending messages to the penis, which makes it difficult for men to achieve or maintain erections.

3. Painful Intercourse

For women, dehydration can cause vaginal dryness, leading to discomfort during sex. This can reduce pleasure and make intimacy a less enjoyable experience.

4. Hormonal Imbalance

Water plays a role in maintaining hormonal balance. Low blood volume can cause dehydration, which can disrupt hormone production. A lack of hormone production leads to mood swings, stress, and reduced sexual interest.

5. Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs)

Not drinking enough water can increase the risk of urinary tract infections. UTIs can be painful and interfere with sexual activity. Staying hydrated helps flush out bacteria and maintain urinary health.

Tips for Staying Hydrated for Better Sexual Health

  • Make at least 3.5 liters of water throughout the day as a habit to maintain overall health and sexual performance.
  • Include fruits and vegetables like watermelon, cucumbers, and oranges in your diet to boost hydration. Also, include all the other water-rich fruits and vegetables.
  • Alcohol and caffeine can dehydrate the body. So, limiting them can help in avoiding dehydration. If you are consuming them, then ensure you drink extra water to balance your hydration levels.
  • If you feel thirsty, don’t ignore it. Thirst is a sign that your body needs water.
  • Hydrate your body before and after, meaning in workouts or any strenuous activities. This helps to replenish lost fluids to maintain good circulation and stamina.

Takeaway

Water is essential for overall well-being, and it also influences sexual health by giving numerous benefits to both men and women. Also, not drinking enough water makes us dehydrate, and that dehydration could lead to erectile dysfunction. Eat water-rich foods and drink sufficient water to enjoy a healthy sexual life. The trend of using royal honey packs has been booming because of the trending short videos on all social media platforms. We need to discuss why we should not use royal honey first, followed by what royal honey does sexually. Because we never recommend using royal honey.

Why is Royal Honey Considered Dangerous?

Royal honey is not recommended for use as it contains tadalafil, which is the active ingredient found in prescription drugs such as Viagra and Cialis, which are used to treat erectile dysfunction (ED). Tadalafil is effective when prescribed and monitored by a healthcare professional. But, its inclusion in royal honey products poses serious risks.

This inclusion of tadalafil in royal honey products has been found and exposed to the public by the FDA. The FDA added the selling of royal honey products under medical fraud.

Why is Tadalafil Dangerous in Royal Honey?

  • The concentration of tadalafil in royal honey is not regulated, which can lead to an overdose. The overdose of tadalafil can cause severe side effects such as headaches, dizziness, chest pain, and dangerously low blood pressure.
  • Tadalafil can interact negatively with other medications that you intake, that too, particularly nitrates. Nitrates are commonly prescribed for heart conditions, and their interference with tadalafil can result in life-threatening drops in blood pressure.
  • Individuals with pre-existing conditions such as heart disease, hypertension, or diabetes are at a higher risk of experiencing adverse effects when using royal honey as it contains tadalafil.

Why Should You Avoid Royal Honey?

1. Misleading Marketing

The term “royal honey” gives the impression of a natural, organic product, but this is misleading. Consumers are often unaware of the inclusion of synthetic drugs like tadalafil, which undermines the product’s credibility and safety.

2. Lack of Regulation

Regulatory bodies like the FDA do not approve Royal honey products. This means there is no guarantee of their safety, quality, or consistency. Unsuspecting users may consume harmful substances without realizing the risks involved.

3. Severe Side Effects

As mentioned earlier, the unregulated presence of tadalafil can lead to severe side effects, including,

  • Cardiovascular issues: Low blood pressure, irregular heartbeat, and heart attacks.
  • Neurological symptoms: Headaches, dizziness, and fainting.
  • Gastrointestinal problems: Nausea, vomiting, and stomach discomfort.

4. Legal and Ethical Concerns

Selling products containing undisclosed pharmaceutical ingredients is illegal in many countries. Using such products can inadvertently support unethical practices and potentially expose users to legal risks.

What Does Royal Honey Do Sexually?

Royal honey has been marketed as a product that boosts libido, enhances sexual performance, and provides prolonged energy. These benefits of using royal honey are only claimed due to the presence of tadalafil and it does facilitate erections by increasing blood flow. 

But the presence of tadalafil can outweigh the potential benefits of the royal honey products. You may have good temporary effects and very bad long term risks associated with royal honey.

Temporary Effects vs. Long-Term Risks

  • Temporary Effects: Improved erection and stamina.
  • Long-Term Risks: Dependence, tolerance, and potential damage to cardiovascular and sexual health.

Psychological Dependence

Suppose you are relying on products like royal honey for sexual performance. In that case, it can lead to psychological dependence and make natural sexual function even more challenging by creating anxiety and lower self-confidence.

Safer Alternatives to Royal Honey

If you are experiencing sexual performance issues, there are a lot of other safer ways to solve the problem. Avoid using royal honey and follow the below-mentioned alternatives.

1. Consult a Healthcare Professional

A qualified and experienced men’s sexual health expert can diagnose the problem and give you the best-tailored treatment to solve the sexual issue without causing any health complications.

2. Natural Supplements

You can use several natural supplements that are available for solving sexual performance issues, such as ginseng, L-arginine, and maca root. However, even if you are opting for natural supplements it is essential to consult a healthcare provider before trying any supplement.

3. Healthy Lifestyle Changes

  • Exercise regularly to improve circulation and overall stamina.
  • Make a diet that has nutrient-rich foods that support hormonal balance and energy levels.
  • Having stress can negatively impact sexual health. So, practice stress-free exercises and meditations.
  • Quitting both alcohol and smoking can help you improve your sexual performance. 

Takeaway

Royal honey is not a natural supplement as it contains a pharmaceutical ingredient, tadalafil. The inclusion of tadalafil can give you temporary instant benefits, but it has serious and very dangerous health complications associated with it in long-term usage. So, use safer, evidence-based approaches to address sexual health concerns instead of unverified products like royal honey. html:
Anastrozole is a medication developed to treat breast cancer in postmenopausal women. But now suggested by most men’s sexual health doctors in managing hormonal imbalances in men. Also, most men take Anastrozole off the label without consulting any men’s sexual health experts. 

This increased attention to Anastrozole is because it improves men’s health by making the balance between testosterone and estrogen. Read this blog post to learn about the benefits, recommended dosages, and potential side effects of Anastrozole for men. 

What is Anastrozole?

Anastrozole is an aromatase inhibitor that blocks the enzyme aromatase because aromatase is present in the testicles, fat cells and livers of our body and converts testosterone into estradiol. 

Simply put, Anastrozole is a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor used in men to maintain a balance between testosterone and estrogen, which is crucial for optimal health. Elevated estrogen levels can lead to issues like gynecomastia (male breast enlargement), and reduced testosterone production causes infertility. 

Why is Anastrozole Prescribed for Men?

This is because Anastrozole can help maintain the balance between testosterone and estrogen. So it can be used for treating various men’s health problems that are listed below,

  • Gynecomastia Management: Excess estrogen can lead to the development of breast tissue in men. Anastrozole is used in such situations as it reduces estrogen levels.
  • Support During Testosterone Therapy: Men undergoing testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) may experience increased estrogen levels as a side effect. So, Anastrozole is used to ensure the effectiveness of TRT.
  • Fertility Treatment: High estrogen levels can suppress sperm production. Anastrozole’s ability to reduce estrogen can improve sperm quality and count, aiding men facing infertility.
  • Hypogonadism: In conditions where testosterone levels are abnormally low. Anastrozole is used in such situations as it can stimulate testosterone naturally.

Benefits of Anastrozole for Men

The top sections of the blog post comprise all the benefits of Anastrozole. This separate section for benefits also explains the same.

  • Anastrozole’s primary benefit lies in maintaining a healthy balance of testosterone and estrogen. This balance is essential for physical and mental well-being.
  • By reducing excess estrogen, Anastrozole effectively prevents or reduces the enlargement of male breast tissue.
  • Restoring hormonal balance can lead to improved sperm production, making it a valuable option for men experiencing infertility due to high estrogen levels.
  • Anastrozole’s ability to lower estrogen indirectly boosts testosterone production, improving energy levels, libido, and overall vitality.
  • Excessive estrogen in men can lead to compromised bone density. Anastrozole helps maintain bone health by regulating estrogen levels.

Dosage Guidelines for Men

Never self-prescribe Anastrozole. Consultation with a healthcare provider is crucial to avoid complications and ensure proper dosing. Because the dosage of Anastrozole for men depends on the condition being treated and individual hormonal profiles. Some general guidelines are,

  • Standard Dosage: The typical dose for managing estrogen levels in men is 0.5 mg to 1 mg daily. You can sometimes take it as per the doctor’s prescription.
  • Frequency: In some cases, Anastrozole may be taken every other day to minimize side effects and to maintain effectiveness.
  • Monitoring: To determine the optimal dosage, you must regularly monitor estrogen and testosterone levels by taking blood tests.
  • Duration: The treatment duration varies depending on the underlying condition and the patient’s response to the medication. 

Potential Side Effects of Anastrozole

Like any medication, anastrozole can also cause side effects. The side effects are explained in four categories,

  • Rare but Serious Side Effects
  • Allergic Reactions

Common Side Effects

  • Anastrozole might reduce energy levels, and that is a frequent complaint.
  • Some users of anastrozole experience discomfort, particularly in larger joints.
  • Some individuals might experience nausea, vomiting, or stomach upset.

Rare but Serious Side Effects

  • Prolonged use can lead to bone density loss and increase the risk of fractures. 
  • In rare cases, some men may experience changes in blood lipid levels that affect heart health.
  • Depression, anxiety, or mood swings may occur due to hormonal changes.

Allergic Reactions

In rare cases, individuals may develop an allergic response like rash, itching, or difficulty breathing. Immediate medical attention is required in such instances.

Risks of Misuse

Anastrozole’s popularity among bodybuilders and athletes for managing estrogen levels while using anabolic steroids has led to instances of misuse. Such misuse of Anastrozole might cause,

  • Disrupt natural hormonal balance.
  • Lead to severe side effects, including liver damage and cardiovascular issues.

Tips for Safe Use

  • Regular check-ups to monitor hormonal levels, bone density, and overall health are crucial during Anastrozole therapy.
  • A balanced diet, regular exercise, and stress management complement the effects of Anastrozole and promote overall well-being.
  • Never use Anastrozole without a prescription, even if symptoms seem similar to the conditions it treats. Misuse can lead to severe complications.

Takeaway

Anastrozole has proven to be a valuable tool for managing hormonal imbalances in men as it offers benefits such as improved testosterone levels, fertility enhancements, and relief from conditions like gynecomastia. title: Watery Semen and Its Effect on Fertility
seoTitle: Watery Semen and Its Effect on Fertility

html:
Most men stress about watery and thin semen. Sometimes, watery semen may occur due to frequent ejaculation, lifestyle factors, and nutritional deficiencies. But in some cases, watery semen occurs due to low sperm count, which might have a huge impact on fertility. You cannot just look at your semen and say you have a problem. So, continue reading to learn more about what’s going on with your seminal fluid and when to seek professional advice.

What is Watery Semen? 

Semen is a thick white fluid that contains sperm and is crucial for male fertility. Seminal fluid’s consistency can vary, but watery semen often appears thin and less viscous than normal. 

While an occasional episode of watery semen is not a serious issue, the consistent changes could signal issues with sperm production or seminal fluid composition.

Does Watery Semen Affect Fertility?

Watery semen, in some consistent cases, may also indicate a low sperm count or poor sperm quality. Both of these factors can affect a man’s ability to conceive. Because fertility does not only rely on sperm count, it also relies not only on their motility (ability to swim) and morphology (shape). So, if semen lacks the necessary nutrients and proteins, then sperm viability may be compromised and reduce the chances of successful fertilization.

What Causes Watery Semen?

1. Frequent Ejaculation

Ejaculating multiple times within a short period can deplete the body’s sperm reserves and lead to thinner and less dense semen. This is a temporary condition and typically resolves with reduced frequency.

2. Lifestyle Factors

Unhealthy habits like,

  • Smoking
  • Excessive Alcohol Consumption
  • Drug use 
  • Stress
  • Lack of sleep
  • Poor diet 

It can negatively impact semen quality and further contribute to changes in seminal fluid consistency.

3. Nutritional Deficiencies

A lack of essential vitamins and minerals such as zinc, vitamin C, and folate can affect sperm production and seminal fluid composition.

4. Dehydration

Insufficient water intake can make semen less viscous and lead to a watery appearance. Staying hydrated is vital for overall reproductive health.

5. Hormonal Imbalances

Testosterone plays a key role in sperm production. Low testosterone levels or imbalances in other hormones can result in reduced sperm count and cause watery semen.

6. Infections or Inflammation

Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) or inflammation in the reproductive organs, such as the prostate or seminal vesicles, can alter semen consistency.

7. Medical Conditions

Conditions like varicocele (enlarged veins in the scrotum), hypogonadism (low testosterone production), and certain genetic disorders can contribute to watery semen and infertility.

When to Consult a Sexologist for Watery Semen

If you are having some occasional watery semen, then there is no problem. But if you are having persistent changes then you should consult with a specialist.

  • If watery semen persists for several weeks.
  • If you and your partner have been trying to conceive for over a year without success
  • Pain during ejaculation
  • Blood in semen
  • Changes in libido
  • If you suspect a past or current STI

You can consult with a sexologist or urologist. who can perform a thorough evaluation and a semen analysis to determine the underlying cause and recommend appropriate treatment.

Treatments for Watery Semen

Watery semens is treated based on the cause of it. So consulting with a healthcare provider can help you identify the cause of the problem and you can treat it with a tailored approach for restoring semen quality and improving fertility.

1. Lifestyle Modifications

  • Incorporate foods rich in zinc, selenium, omega-3 fatty acids, and antioxidants to boost sperm health.
  • Regular exercise improves blood circulation, and also moderate physical activity improves testosterone levels and overall reproductive health.
  • Avoid bad habits like smoking, alcohol, and drugs. If you can’t quit, then limiting them can help.
  • Avoiding stress is very important as you avoid a bad habit. Practicing relaxation techniques like meditation or yoga to reduce stress levels can help.

2. Hydration and Nutrition

  • Drink plenty of water to maintain hydration levels.
  • Take multivitamins to maintain nutrient levels in the body. You can intake supplements if advised by your healthcare provider.

3. Medical Treatments

  • You can go under hormone therapy like testosterone replacement therapy or other hormonal treatments that your doctor may prescribe.
  • Inflammation caused by any Infections can be treated with appropriate antibiotics.

4. Surgical Interventions

  • Surgery to address varicocele can improve semen quality and sperm production.

5. Fertility Treatments

  • In severe cases, healthcare providers may use techniques like Intrauterine Insemination (IUI) or In Vitro Fertilization (IVF)  to achieve conception.

6. Regular Monitoring

  • Suppose you are having consistent watery semen conditions. Then, consulting with a healthcare provider is necessary, and keeping track of it with regular follow-up is necessary to monitor the treatment.

Conclusion

Watery and thin semen can be a source of concern for many men, but in occasional cases, it is normal, and there are no serious complications with fertility. But if it is persistent, then you may need professional evaluation. To treat watery semen, you need professional guidance as we need to know the cause of the issue. So, if you are experiencing consistent watery semen, then consult with Fortius Health Clinic’s men’s sexologist doctors for treating watery semen.

html:
When a man has his orgasm but does not ejaculate, semen is a condition called dry orgasm. Some individuals do dry orgasm purposefully, but in some cases, it is involuntary. 

Individuals with dry orgasms do not have any difficulty performing sexually as they can maintain an erection, but during the climax, they do not ejaculate. So, this condition may be very challenging and needs to be treated as it has a lack in releasing semen. Keep reading this article to learn more about the causes and available treatments for dry orgasms.

What is Dry orgasm?

A dry orgasm is the orgasm attained by the man without ejaculating any semen but where it feels like a regular orgasm. It is an unharmful condition and also does not affect sexual performance but can affect the chance of making your partner pregnant. 

What Causes Dry Orgasms?

The range of medical conditions, certain medications, and surgical procedures can cause dry orgasms. Here are the most common causes,

  1. Retrograde Ejaculation
  2. Prostate Surgery
  3. Medications
  4. Nerve Damage
  5. Congenital Conditions
  6. Intentional Practices

Retrograde Ejaculation

Normally the semen exists penis, but in retrograde ejaculation, the semen flows back into the bladder. This condition is a frequent cause of dry orgasms, and retrograde ejaculation may be caused due to,

  • Diabetes
  • Neurological disorders
  • Surgery involving the prostate, bladder, or pelvic region
  • Side effects of certain medications, such as alpha-blockers

Prostate Surgery

Procedures like transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) or prostatectomy can disrupt the normal ejaculation process and lead to dry orgasms.

Medications

Certain drugs, which include antidepressants, antihypertensives, and medications for enlarged prostate, can interfere with ejaculation.

Nerve Damage

Injuries to the spinal cord or nerve damage in the pelvic region, which are controlling the ejaculation, may result in dry orgasms.

Congenital Conditions

In very rare cases, some men are born with anatomical abnormalities that cause dry orgasms.

Intentional Practices

Some men deliberately practice techniques to achieve dry orgasms as part of tantric or other sexual practices.

Symptoms of Dry Orgasm

There will be no pain if you have a dry orgasm. Instead, you may notice signs like, 

  • The sensation of climax without the release of semen 
  • Cloudy or discolored urine after orgasm (in cases of retrograde ejaculation)
  • Difficulty achieving pregnancy despite regular sexual activity 
  • A feeling of “something missing” during ejaculation

Does Dry Orgasm Affect Sexual Performance?

One of the key concerns for men experiencing dry orgasms is whether it impacts their sexual performance. Fortunately, most men can maintain an erection and engage in sexual activity without issues. However, the psychological impact of the condition can lead to feelings of inadequacy or anxiety, which may indirectly affect sexual satisfaction.

Is Dry Orgasm a Cause for Concern?

Dry orgasms are not harmful. But, the condition is particularly concerning for couples trying to conceive, as it significantly reduces the likelihood of pregnancy. 

Diagnosing Dry Orgasm

When you are consulting with a health care provider, he will diagnose dry orgasm with a step-by-step process that is mentioned below,

  • The doctors will do a detailed medical history review
  • Physical examination for checking any kind of abnormalities 
  • Semen analysis is done to determine the presence of retrograde ejaculation
  • Urinalysis after orgasm to detect semen in the urine
  • Imaging studies of the ejaculatory system to check the function and structure of the system.

Treatment Options for Dry Orgasm

The treatment for dry orgasms depends on the cause of the condition. Here are some common approaches that are followed to treat dry orgasms. They are,

Medications

  • Alpha-adrenergic agonists like pseudoephedrine may help restore normal ejaculation by improving bladder-neck closure.
  • Switching medications if current prescriptions are causing the condition.

Fertility Treatments

For men trying to conceive then, fertility specialists may recommend,

  • Sperm retrieval techniques to extract viable sperm from the testicles or urine.
  • Assisted reproductive technologies such as IVF or ICSI.

Surgical Intervention

In cases involving anatomical abnormalities or complications from previous surgeries, corrective procedures may be considered.

Lifestyle Modifications

Managing underlying health conditions like diabetes, reducing stress, and improving overall health can positively impact ejaculation function.

Counseling

Psychological support may help men cope with the emotional challenges associated with dry orgasms.

How to Prevent Dry Orgasms?

Preventing dry orgasms involves maintaining good overall health and addressing risk factors. Here are some tips,

  • Manage Chronic Conditions: Keep diabetes, high blood pressure, and other chronic illnesses under control. Regular 
  • Check-Ups: Routine medical examinations can help detect and manage issues early. 
  • Be Informed About Medications: Discuss the potential side effects of prescribed drugs with your doctor. 
  • Avoid Risky Practices: Use protection during sports or physical activities to minimize the risk of nerve damage.

Takeaway

A dry orgasm is a nonharmful, nonpainful condition that does not affect sexual performance. But it can affect the chance of making your partner pregnant and affect you mentally. Testosterone Pellets is one form of testosterone replacement therapy where the small grain sized pellet is implanted under the skin. These testosterone pellets increase the level of testosterone in your body.

The condition called male hypogonadism is increasing in the modern days and the solution to it is testosterone replacement therapy (TRT). There are various ways doctors use to replace testosterone in the body like gel, injection or pellet.

In this particular article we have discussed in detail about the procedure, benefits and side effects of testosterone pellets.   

What are Testosterone Pellets?

Testosterone pellets are one way of increasing the testosterone levels in the body with the help of pellets containing crystalized testosterone placed under the skin near the hip in the size of 3 millimeters (mm).

These pellets placed under the skin slowly release testosterone into the body. The pellets get dissolved in 2- 6 months and need not to be removed. Mostly the testosterone pellets are replaced once in three months to maintain the even testosterone level.

Benefits of Testosterone Pellets

Testosterone pellets offer several advantages when compared with other forms of testosterone replacement therapy (TRT). They are,

1. Long-Lasting Effects

Testosterone pellets provide a steady release of testosterone for 3 to 6 months. Which is a very long lasting one when compared with daily gels or weekly injections.  This consistency helps avoid the hormonal fluctuations that can occur with other methods, reducing mood swings and maintaining even energy levels.

2. Convenience

Once testosterone pellets have been implanted they do not need daily upkeep like gel or injection. As you need to remember to apply a gel or schedule frequent doctor visits for injections. 

3. Improved Symptoms of Hypogonadism

The symptoms of hypogonadism improve. So you could see increased energy, better libido, enhanced muscle mass, reduced fat accumulation, Improved mood and cognitive function.

4. Consistent Hormone Levels

Testosterone pellets release the hormone gradually into the bloodstream and so it maintains more stable testosterone levels compared to injections or gels. This also ensures not spiking the testosterone levels to the peak and avoiding complications.

5. Minimal Skin Irritation

In case of gels it may cause skin irritations or require careful application to avoid transferring to others. Testosterone pellets pose no such risks once implanted.

6. Discreet and Hidden

The small size and subdermal placement make the pellets virtually invisible. And needed to be removed as the pellets placed under the skin dissolve completely.

Side Effects of Testosterone Pellets

While testosterone pellets are generally safe, they can have side effects. Understanding these potential issues helps ensure you make an informed decision.

1. Implantation Site Reactions

Some individuals may experience redness, swelling, or bruising at the implantation site. In rare cases like not taking care well after the procedure could cause infection or pellet extrusion can occur.

2. Hormonal Side Effects

  • Acne: Increased testosterone levels may trigger acne or oily skin.
  • Hair Loss: Those genetically predisposed to male-pattern baldness may notice accelerated hair thinning.
  • Mood Changes: Some individuals may experience irritability or mood swings due to hormonal shifts.

3. Risk of Overproduction

If the dosage is too high, it can lead to excessive testosterone levels, resulting in side effects such as increased red blood cell count (polycythemia) or sleep apnea.

4. Rare Systemic Effects

Though uncommon, some people report headaches, joint pain, or fluid retention. These side effects often resolve as the body adjusts to the therapy.

5. Long-Term Risks

Prolonged high testosterone levels may potentially increase the risk of heart disease or prostate issues. Regular monitoring by a healthcare provider is essential.

Dosage of Testosterone Pellets

Choosing the correct dosage is needed as the more and low dosage could cause complications. Consult with your healthcare provider to know the even dosage. Never miss any dose of pellets after the one set gets dissolved.  

How Testosterone Pellets Are Placed

The doctors take time only to find the right dosage of testosterone needed for you and the implant of testosterone pellets are performed in a clinic in just 10 minutes.

  • Doctors clean and sterilize the implantation site i.e. usually your upper hip or buttock area. 
  • Local anesthetic is injected to numb the area to make the procedure painless.
  • The doctor inserts the pellets just beneath the skin using a specialized medical instrument called trocar.
  • Then nearly 10 -12 pellets are placed and the procedure is redone when the pellets dissolve.

Post Procedure care and Follow up

Post procedure care and follow up with doctors appointment after the implantation of testosterone pellets is unavoidable as it has a lot of risks and side effects associated with it.

  • The site is covered with a bandage to protect it during healing.
  • Patients are advised to avoid heavy lifting or strenuous activity for a few days.
  • Keep the area clean and dry to prevent infection.

Takeaway

Testosterone pellets are the slowest and most recommended method by the medical professionals for increasing the levels of testosterone. The dosage needed for you is very important as the over dosage of testosterone could cause health complications. Thus consult a male sexual health clinic to choose the right dosage and implantation of testosterone pallets.

What is Edging in Sex?

Edging in sex is a technique used by both individuals or a couple to intentionally delay orgasm by reaching the edge of climax and then backing off. This process is repeated multiple times before finally allowing the orgasm to occur. Edging technique in sex is also known as “peaking” or “surfing”.

Edging is a natural and non-harmful method used to enhance sexual pleasure, prolong the experience, and make the climax more intense. The edging technique in sex is versatile, as it can be practised during masturbation or partnered sexual activities.

html:
Everyone may know that most of the men in this modern era experience difficulty in ejaculation as they get older. But the answer to this most popular question, “At what age does a man stop ejaculating?” is not precise because the answer to this question depends on several medical and psychological factors.

Ejaculation is an essential part of the male reproductive system. So, understanding at what age a man stops ejaculating and the reasons behind it is very important. 

A survey shows that 40 percent of people aged between 65 and 80 are sexually active. This survey and some other studies on the internet prove that there is no particular age where a man stops ejaculating. So stop the negative thinking and explore this article by Fortius Health Clinic as it explains when you should worry about ejaculation problems as you get older, along with the steps to be taken to prevent them.

At What Age Does A Man Stop Ejaculating?

There is no specific age where every man stops ejaculation. The age at which a man stops ejaculating depends on the several health complications that lead to difficulty in ejaculation. 

The myth here is that as you get older, you will not be able to ejaculate because there are proven studies. Among them is one study that shows men are more sexually active than women, also, it proves more than one-third of men aged 85 are having a good quality sex life.

Factors That Affect Ejaculation as Men Age

Not only men’s sexual health complications related to ejaculation, like erectile dysfunction, premature ejaculation, or penile problems, are factors that stop ejaculation as men age. There are several factors that you might not think of, like spinal cord injury and habits like excessive smoking and drinking are also played as factors that might stop ejaculation as you age. 

Because a complex interplay of physical, hormonal, and psychological factors influences ejaculation. So, we have mentioned the key factors that can affect ejaculation to make you aware,

  • Hormonal changes
  • Health Conditions
  • Medications
  • Neurological Factors
  • Psychological and Emotional Factors
  • Lifestyle Habits
  • Age-Related Physical Changes
  • Surgical Procedures

Hormonal Changes

  • Testosterone Decline: Testosterone levels naturally decrease with age, which can influence libido, sexual function, and ejaculatory capability.
  • Andropause: The male equivalent of menopause may result in decreased sexual performance, although its effects vary between individuals.

Health Conditions

  • Prostate Problems: Conditions such as benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) or prostate surgery can interfere with ejaculation. 
  • Diabetes: High blood sugar levels can damage nerves, leading to retrograde ejaculation or reduced ejaculatory sensation. 
  • Cardiovascular Diseases: Reduced blood flow due to heart-related issues can lead to erectile dysfunction, which can indirectly affect ejaculation.

Medications

Certain medications, such as antidepressants, blood pressure drugs, and prostate treatments, can cause delayed ejaculation or inhibit it altogether.

Neurological Factors

  • Nerve Damage: Injuries or conditions such as multiple sclerosis or Parkinson’s disease can impair the neural pathways responsible for ejaculation. 
  • Spinal Cord Injuries: Depending on the severity and location, spinal cord injuries can significantly impact ejaculation.

Psychological and Emotional Factors

  • Stress and Anxiety: Mental health challenges, such as performance anxiety or relationship issues, can affect sexual function. 
  • Depression: Low mood and lack of interest in sexual activity can lead to reduced ejaculation frequency or difficulty.

Lifestyle Habits

  • Smoking and Alcohol: These habits, like smoking and alcohol consumption, can harm blood vessels and nerve function, leading to sexual health issues. 
  • Obesity: Excessive weight can cause hormonal imbalances and increase the risk of conditions like diabetes, which affect ejaculation.

Age-Related Physical Changes

  • Reduced Muscle Tone: The muscles involved in ejaculation may weaken with age, leading to less forceful or delayed ejaculation. 
  • Erectile Dysfunction (ED): Difficulty maintaining an erection can impact the ability to ejaculate effectively.

Surgical Procedures

  • Prostate Surgery: Procedures such as TURP (transurethral resection of the prostate) or radical prostatectomy can lead to retrograde ejaculation or loss of ejaculation. 
  • Pelvic Surgeries: Operations in the pelvic region may damage nerves or muscles related to ejaculation.

Steps to Prevent Ejaculation Problems as You Age

  1. Maintain a balanced diet rich in essential nutrients for hormonal and vascular health. You can boost testosterone with food.
  2. Exercise regularly to improve blood circulation and boost overall fitness. 
  3. Stay hydrated to support proper bodily functions, including sexual health. 
  4. Manage stress through relaxation techniques like yoga or meditation. 
  5. Avoid smoking and limit alcohol consumption to protect your vascular and nervous systems. 
  6. Get enough sleep to ensure optimal hormone production and energy levels. 
  7. Maintain a healthy weight to reduce the risk of lifestyle-related health issues. 
  8. Regularly monitor and manage chronic health conditions like diabetes and hypertension. 
  9. Communicate openly with your partner to reduce performance anxiety and emotional stress. 
  10. Visit a healthcare professional for regular check-ups and early management of potential issues.

Takeaway


There is no fixed age where a man stops his ejaculation. So, the answer to the question depends on several factors that make ejaculation difficult as you age. So following the preventive methods to maintain a healthy life in order to avoid health complications that make ejaculation difficult. Consulting men’s sexual doctors is recommended to find and solve serious health complications.

Masturbation is not wrong because it’s safe when done correctly. But when you are holding too tight or doing it too fast, then it can lead to desensitization, and it is called death grip syndrome. What is Death Grip Syndrome?

Death grip syndrome is a situation where a man finds masturbation an easier way to get an orgasm than having sex with his partner. Death grip syndrome is a term used by slang and not taken from any medical textbooks. 

In simple terms, if you are finding it easy to reach the climax through masturbation and finding it difficult through sex with a partner, then you are having death grip syndrome.

Is death grip syndrome really a thing?

Yes, it is really a thing and also not new. Because when a person does hyperstimulation, it may lead them to desensitization of their penis. Death grip syndrome is also prevalent because research shows that when a person gets more satisfaction through masturbation, then he will choose a deep-rooted, unique, bad masturbation technique.

Symptoms of Death Grip Syndrome

Recognizing the symptoms of DGS is the first step toward addressing it. Common symptoms of death grip syndrome include

  1. Reduced Sensitivity: Genitals may feel numb or less responsive to physical touch during partnered sexual activities. 
  2. Delayed or Inhibited Climax: Difficulty achieving orgasm or needing prolonged stimulation to climax. 
  3. Preference for Specific Stimulation: Dependence on a particular technique or pressure that cannot be easily replicated during sexual activity with a partner. 
  4. Erectile Dysfunction: You might have challenges in maintaining an erection due to insufficient arousal during intimate encounters. 
  5. Frustration or Anxiety: Emotional distress stemming from dissatisfaction with sexual performance or inability to connect with a partner. 
  6. Decreased Sexual Confidence: Fear of being unable to perform or satisfy a partner, leading to avoidance of intimacy.

Causes of Death Grip Syndrome

Understanding the root causes of DGS can help individuals prevent or address the condition effectively. Key contributing factors include

  1. Excessive Pressure: Using an overly tight grip during masturbation can desensitize the nerve endings in the penis. 
  2. Fast or Aggressive Techniques: Rushing through self-stimulation can train the body to require intense, rapid stimulation to achieve arousal or climax. 
  3. Overstimulation: Frequent masturbation, especially without proper recovery time, can lead to physical fatigue and nerve desensitization. 
  4. Psychological Factors: Anxiety, stress, or guilt associated with masturbation can worsen the symptoms. 
  5. Porn-Induced Stimulation: Over-reliance on explicit material can lead to unrealistic expectations, affecting arousal in real-life scenarios.

How to Fix Death Grip Syndrome

  • Take a break
  • Change Techniques
  • Focus on partnered intimacy.
  • Practice Mindful Masturbation

Take a Break

Giving your body time to recover is one of the simplest yet most effective ways to reset sensitivity. Temporarily abstain from masturbation for a few weeks or reduce its frequency significantly.

Change Techniques

Experiment with lighter grip pressure or slower stimulation to retrain your body. This helps restore sensitivity and allows for a more natural response to touch.

Focus on Partnered Intimacy

Prioritize intimate moments with your partner to rewire your sexual response. Engage in open communication about your preferences and explore new ways of connection.

Practice Mindful Masturbation

Pay attention to the sensations and avoid rushing. Use lubrication to reduce friction and create a more natural experience.

Limit Pornography Consumption

Reduce reliance on pornography to avoid unrealistic expectations. Engage with your partner or practice imagining sensual scenarios instead.

Pelvic Floor Exercises

By strengthening your pelvic floor muscles with Kegel exercises you can enhance your control and improve sexual performance over time.

Seek Professional Help

If symptoms persist or cause significant distress, consult a healthcare provider or sexual health specialist. At Fortius Health Clinic, our experts are experienced in helping individuals overcome DGS with personalized treatment plans and counseling.

Preventing Death Grip Syndrome

Prevention is always better than cure. Here are a few tips to ensure a healthy masturbation routine

  • Moderation: Avoid excessive frequency or overly long sessions. 
  • Proper Technique: Use gentle, varied stimulation instead of repetitive, forceful motions. 
  • Regular Breaks: Allow your body time to recover between sessions. 
  • Healthy Lifestyle: Follow a healthy lifestyle by Maintaining a balanced diet, exercising regularly, and managing stress levels to support overall sexual health.

When to Seek Help

Death Grip Syndrome is not a medical emergency. Still, it can significantly affect your sexual confidence and relationships. If you experience persistent symptoms or find it challenging to enjoy intimacy even after following the reverse techniques, then seeking professional help is recommended. 

Takeaway

Masturbation is a healthy and natural practice, but it’s essential to do it responsibly to prevent desensitization and its associated challenges. html:
Clomid (clomiphene citrate) is an FDA-approved fertility drug used to treat female infertility and not approved by the FDA to treat male fertility. But it’s often prescribed by male sexual doctors off-label to treat male infertility as Clomid for men can increase their testosterone and sperm count. 

Clomid is a popular brand name and nickname of clomiphene citrate. If you’re a man looking to know more about Clomid, like what it is, how it works, and what the side effects of using it are. Then, read this blog post. Also, this blog will teach you how important it is to consult with a doctor before using clomid.

What is Clomid (clomiphene citrate)?

Clomid is a brand name of clomiphene citrate. It is an oral medication suggested for hormonal imbalance-related female fertility issues and is also approved by the FDA for female fertility problems. It comes under a class of drugs called selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERM). 

Is Clomid Prescribed For Men?

Yes, Clomid is prescribed off the label for men who are all affected by fertility problems. Clomid is mostly suggested for those who have low sperm counts due to low testosterone levels. 

A meta-analysis conducted by the National Library Of Medicine in 2023 proves that clomid is a safe therapy for male infertility. This study shows that intake of clomiphene citrate increases sperm concentration and sperm motility.

How Does Clomid Work for Men?

Clomid creates a “false low estrogen” environment in the brain by blocking the receptor called the hypothalamus (the brain’s control center for reproductive hormone regulation). That’s why it falls under the drug list selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM). 

Due to low estrogen levels, the hypothalamus signals the pituitary gland to release two critical hormones 

  • Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH)
  • Luteinizing Hormone (LH)

In men, these hormones help in producing testosterone and sperm. It increases sperm concentration and sperm motility, which is very crucial for sperm development.

Can Clomid cause twins?

Yes, Clomid could cause twins. But it does not guarantee that you will have twins. However, the chances of twins remain relatively low, with studies showing about a 7-10% likelihood of twin pregnancies when using Clomid.

How Long Does it Take for a Clomid to Increase Sperm Count?

Clomid for men does not have enough studies on how many days it takes for sperm production, and it works in the ejaculation process. It varies from person to person. Mostly, it will take more than 3-4 months to see the optimal effect of clomid in men. 

When it comes to women, the clomid starts to work in 7-10 days. We can assure you that, but for men, it is better to consult with a healthcare provider so that they can do testing to assure you that the clomid is working. 

Signs Clomid Is Working in Men

We have listed some of the signs of Clomid that you may notice when it is working effectively.

  • Increased Testosterone Levels: Blood tests show a rise in testosterone, often within 3-4 months of starting treatment. 
  • Improved Sperm Count: Semen analysis indicates higher sperm concentration and better motility. 
  • Enhanced Libido: Noticeable improvement in sex drive and overall sexual function. 
  • Reduced Fatigue: Increased energy levels and reduced symptoms of low testosterone. 
  • Improved Mood: Reduced irritability, depression, or mood swings often associated with hormonal imbalance. 
  • Physical Changes: Signs like improved muscle mass, reduced body fat, or decreased breast tissue (gynecomastia). 
  • Better Fertility Outcomes: Partners achieving pregnancy can confirm Clomid’s effectiveness.

What Dosage of Clomid should be taken by men?

Clomid usually comes as a 50 mg tablet. However, for men, only 25mg is needed per day, so taking one tablet in two days is recommended.  High doses of Clomid by men can lead to excessive stimulation of the hypothalamus and pituitary gland, which causes a hormonal imbalance that may result in negative side effects.

Side Effects of Clomid in Men

Clomid can be effective in treating male infertility and hormonal imbalances. But it may also cause certain side effects. They are categorized and listed below.

Common Side Effects

  • Mood Changes: Irritability, anxiety, or depression.
  • Headaches: Mild to moderate headaches are frequently reported.
  • Fatigue: Feeling tired or experiencing low energy.
  • Hot Flashes: Episodes of sweating or feeling unusually warm.
  • Nausea: Occasional gastrointestinal discomfort.

Hormonal-Related Side Effects

  • Gynecomastia: Enlargement or tenderness of breast tissue due to increased estrogen levels.
  • Reduced Libido: Decreased sexual drive in some cases.
  • Acne or Skin Issues: Caused by hormonal changes.

Reproductive Effects

  • Changes in Sperm Quality: While Clomid often improves sperm production, in rare cases, it may negatively impact sperm motility or morphology.

Vision Disturbances

  • Blurred vision, floaters, or increased light sensitivity may occur but are generally reversible.

Rare Side Effects

  • Weight Gain: Uncommon but possible due to changes in metabolism or hormone levels. 
  • Blood Clots: Rare but serious, requiring immediate medical attention.

If side effects become severe or persist, it is essential to consult with a healthcare professional to adjust the dosage or explore alternative treatments.

Takeaway

Clomid has minimal studies done based on men. However, the available studies have proven that it is a safe therapy to increase testosterone and sperm levels in men. If you are facing fertility issues, never take clomid at your own risk. Always consult with a male sexologist to get tailored treatment solutions. It also helps you to avoid side effects.

html:
Hyperspermia is a condition where a man produces a higher volume of semen during ejaculation. Hyperspermia is the opposite of hypospermia, where a man produces less semen during ejaculation. Only very few are affected by hyperspermia when compared to hypospermia. Knowing all about hyperspermia, like its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, and treatments, is important for an individual affected by hyperspermia and for those who are interested in men’s sexual health. We have discussed that all in this blog post.

What is Hyperspermia?

Hyperspermia is a condition that refers to the production of an unusually larger amount of semen per ejaculation than the usual amount. Variations in semen volume can occur naturally. But, hyperspermia is relatively uncommon and may have implications for sexual health and fertility.

What Causes Hyperspermia?

The exact causes of hyperspermia are not fully understood, and no research has proven the cause of hyperspermia. However, there are some factors listed below that may contribute to higher semen production. They are,

  • Lifestyle
  • Hormonal levels
  • Genetics
  • High fluid intake
  • Prolonged periods between ejaculations
  • Certain health supplements

How Does Hyperspermia Affect Fertility?

While hyperspermia often does not negatively impact fertility. In some very rare cases hyperspermia affected individuals may have lower sperm concentration in the semen they produce. Due to low sperm concentration, it may be difficult for them to fertilize their partner’s egg.

If you have high semen and average sperm concentration, then it could not affect fertility.

How to Induce Hyperspermia

Some people may be interested in increasing semen volume for various reasons. Here are some factors that contribute to increased semen production. They are,

  • Hydration
  • A balanced diet
  • Regular exercises
  • Specific supplements like zinc and amino acids

However, medical consultation is recommended to avoid adverse effects.

Is Hyperspermia Real?

Yes, hyperspermia is a recognized medical condition where an individual produces more semen than usual. It is a very rare condition when compared with any other condition. Hyperspermia is best understood through a medical evaluation to ensure there are no underlying health concerns.

When to Consult a Doctor for Hyperspermia

If you’re having pain or discomfort or if you are having concerns regarding fertility, then consulting a men’s sexual health professional is advised. 

How to Know if You Have Hyperspermia

Semen analysis is the most reliable way to determine whether you are experiencing hyperspermia. This test measures semen volume, sperm concentration, and overall sperm health. If the volume consistently exceeds 5 milliliters per ejaculation, then it is confirmed that you are experiencing hyperspermia.

How is Hyperspermia Diagnosed?

When you have hyperspermia, the healthcare professional may follow some of the primary steps during the diagnosis. They are,

  • Medical History and Symptoms Discussion
  • Physical Examination
  • Semen Analysis
  • Semen Volume
  • Sperm Concentration, Motility and Morphology
  • Hormone Testing
  • Imaging Studies

Medical History and Symptoms Discussion

A healthcare provider first reviews any reported symptoms, frequency of ejaculation, lifestyle habits, and medical history to determine if there might be underlying factors influencing semen volume.

Physical Examination

A urologist or men’s health specialist might conduct a physical exam, especially focusing on the reproductive organs, to rule out any anatomical issues, infections, or conditions affecting the seminal vesicles and prostate.

Semen Analysis

This is the key diagnostic tool for hyperspermia. In a semen analysis, a sample is collected and tested to measure semen volume. If the volume exceeds 5 milliliters per ejaculation, then the presence of hyperspermia is confirmed.

Sperm Concentration, Motility and Morphology

While hyperspermia involves increased semen volume, the semen may also have lower sperm concentration. So, the ejaculated semen is analyzed to find out the sperm concentration. Also, these tests evaluate the sperm’s ability to move and shape, which will help doctors assess if increased semen volume is affecting sperm quality.

Hormone Testing

Blood tests may be performed to measure testosterone, follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), and luteinizing hormone (LH) levels. Hormonal imbalances, particularly those involving testosterone or other hormones that influence reproductive health, can sometimes lead to changes in semen production.

Imaging Studies

In rare cases, doctors might perform imaging studies such as an ultrasound to check for abnormalities in the seminal vesicles or prostate that could lead to increased semen production.

By compiling the results at the end of the diagnosis a healthcare provider can confirm hyperspermia presence and better understand to provide a treatment for you.

How is Hyperspermia Treated?

While hyperspermia typically does not require treatment unless it is causing discomfort or fertility issues or is linked to an underlying medical condition, certain treatment options may be considered based on individual needs. Here are common treatment approaches

Lifestyle Modifications

Simple changes in lifestyle can sometimes help manage hyperspermia, particularly if it is related to external factors.

  • Hydration Balance: While hydration is essential, reducing excess fluid intake may help regulate semen volume.
  • Frequency of Ejaculation: For some, increasing ejaculation frequency may help stabilize semen volume over time.

Nutritional Supplements

For men looking to optimize their semen volume for fertility purposes, some may benefit from specific supplements that support reproductive health, such as

  • Zinc and Selenium: Known to support sperm production and reproductive function.
  • Amino Acids and L-carnitine: Often recommended for sperm health, these can also impact semen volume.
  • Folic Acid: Although primarily known for its role in DNA synthesis, folic acid can support sperm health and motility, potentially indirectly affecting semen volume.

Hormonal Therapy

If hyperspermia is linked to hormonal imbalances, a healthcare provider may suggest hormone therapy. Adjusting testosterone or other hormone levels can help regulate semen production. This approach requires careful monitoring and is tailored to individual hormonal profiles.

Treatment of Underlying Conditions

If hyperspermia is due to an underlying condition, treating that condition can help regulate semen volume. For example,

  • Infections: Bacterial or viral infections affecting the reproductive organs can lead to changes in semen production. Treating the infection with antibiotics or antivirals can often resolve the issue.
  •  Prostate or Seminal Vesicle Disorders: In cases where abnormalities in these glands lead to hyperspermia, medical or surgical intervention may be recommended.

Takeaway

Hyperspermia is a less discussed topic in the men’s sexual health field as it only affects very few people when compared with other men’s sexual conditions. Consulting a men’s sexual expert is necessary as sometimes, in very rare cases, hyperspermia could cause low sperm concentration in semen, which might end in fertility.
